findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass the password check
findings.body: The password check is skipped whenever `credentials.totpCode` is set (line 121). The backup-code branch only checks `twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode`. The password check is conditioned only on `totpCode` being absent, so it still runs when a backupCode is sent without a totpCode. But an attacker who sends both `totpCode` (any value) and a valid `backupCode` skips the password check and logs in with only a backup code. With no totpCode, backup-code login would need the password, which is the intended behavior. The skip condition should not be satisfiable by an arbitrary `totpCode` string.

findings.title: Non-constant-time backup code comparison with no single-use check for nulls
findings.body: `indexOf` on the decrypted array compares codes with plain equality. Used codes are replaced with `null`, which is fine. Rate limiting on this path is only the generic per-email limit. The read-modify-write of the encrypted array is not atomic, so two concurrent logins with the same code can both succeed before the update lands and the code is consumed twice.

findings.title: Backup code type not validated and not consumed
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` throws a 500 if backupCode is not a string, for example a number or object. There is no rate limit on this endpoint, so a session holder with the password can brute-force the codes. If a backupCode is sent with a stale `code`, the backup branch takes precedence, which can be confusing.

findings.title: Backup codes overwritten on every setup call
findings.body: Setup regenerates and overwrites backup codes each time it is called while 2FA is not yet enabled. If the user abandons the flow, stale codes remain stored. Codes are returned before the TOTP is verified, so the client holds codes for a not-yet-enabled 2FA. The codes are shown only after enabling, so a user who closes the modal early or reloads loses them with no regenerate option.

findings.title: Backup codes dialog can be dismissed, and state is not fully reset
findings.body: After enabling, the close button calls `onEnable` and `resetState`, but `backupCodes` and the blob URL are never cleared or revoked after close. The codes stay in React state, and the object URL leaks. Clicking outside the dialog (`onOpenChange`) bypasses the codes screen, so the user may never see their codes.

findings.title: Component misnamed TwoFactor
findings.body: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, which duplicates the name of the other component and is misleading.

findings.title: No tests for backup code login or disable
findings.body: Backup-code login and disable are untested, as the TODO admits. The copy and download assertions do not check content. The new security-sensitive logic has no coverage.
